options.counterfactual: For some r at least three, S_r contains zero: a fixed graph H can have ex(n,H)=t_r(n)+O(1) while admitting no simultaneous edge- and cycle-maximizer for infinitely many orders.
options.approach: Examine bounded perturbations of complete r-partite graphs, allowing both added internal edges and deleted cross-edges. Compare their edge counts and cycle expansions to identify how a bounded-surplus counterexample could escape the usual first-order comparison.

options.approach: Separate a universal lower bound on admissible coefficients from the construction of counterexamples approaching that bound. This would distinguish a genuinely open endpoint from a threshold attained by one fixed forbidden graph.
